Use case: precise-object-edit. Carefully correct the central chest-and-carriers portion of the provided Episode 11 miniature. Preserve the exact existing Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript style, rich lapis/malachite/vermilion/antique-gold palette, fine floral fabrics, painterly egg-tempera texture and soft aged ivory vellum vignette. Keep the horizontal framing and request EXACT same1586×992 pixel canvas.

Essential physical correction:
Replace the current undersized, shallow, awkward-lidded box with ONE large, believable wooden sea-chest long and deep enough to contain a whole living adult woman comfortably seated or partly reclining. It should read as a substantial PERSON-SIZED travel chest, roughly adult body length, with coherent rectangular construction, one clearly visible deep interior, four corners in consistent perspective, and ONE SINGLE THIN HINGED LID opened toward the rear at about60–75 degrees. There must be NO second lid, no doubled upper rim or floating stacked wooden panel. Hands of the carriers grip the side carry handles or support the chest base, never a separate lid.

Show Nestan clearly SEATED INSIDE the open front/top of this large sea-chest. Her face, neck, shoulders, torso and both arms must form ONE continuous anatomically coherent adult body. Her bent knees and folded emerald-gold skirt lie inside the chest, with enough visible interior space to explain the rest of her body. The near front wall may be low enough and the viewpoint high enough to reveal her upper body and the fabric-covered bent legs. NO tiny disembodied head or isolated hand sticking out of a slot; NO severed-body illusion; NO second Nestan; NO body intersecting wooden walls. Keep her recognizable young olive face, dark eyes, black-and-gold head veil, emerald diadem and green-gold dress. She is alive, alert and distressed.

Exactly TWO unnamed male servants in DARK CHARCOAL / DEEP UMBER ROBES carry this single large chest down the stone steps toward the small rowing boat at the right. The servants are strong full adult figures at believable scale relative to Nestan, each carrying one end with natural hand contact, coordinated posture and grounded feet. Replace the original bright blue/ochre robes with dark robes and simple dark cloth caps; no armor.

Preserve Davar at the palace arch on the left, commanding with her outstretched hand, stern maroon-and-gold hood, face and location unchanged. Preserve the same sheltered coastline, waiting plain wooden rowing boat, palace in the distance, floral pomegranates, rocky steps, all decorative style and scene lighting. Exactly FOUR people total: Davar, Nestan and two dark-robed servants. No Tariel, Parsadan or other figures. This is one continuous forced embarkation moment, no suicide inset and no graphic violence.

Use case: illustration-story.
Medieval Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript miniature painting illustrating Episode 11 of Shota Rustaveli's "The Knight in the Panther's Skin" (ვეფხისტყაოსანი): Davar's Wrath & the Casting of Nestan Out to Sea.
Setting: India, the seaward exit of the royal palace and a small waiting boat on the shore.
Scene: Davar gestures in stern fury from the palace gateway while two unnamed attendants carry a large wooden chest toward a waiting boat. The lid remains sufficiently open to show Nestan’s distressed face and green veil, conveying her forced removal without graphic violence. The palace gateway, descending stone path and nearby sheltered shore all belong to ONE continuous place and moment. Two unnamed adult male attendants, in simple medieval tunics and cloth caps, carry a very large rectangular wooden travel chest with brass hinges. The slightly lifted lid and Nestan's visible upper face, black veil and green shoulder show that this is a forced removal of a living captive. She looks distressed and alert. The chest is plainly a cargo/travel chest, NOT a coffin. At the left, Davar at the palace gateway directs them away with a severe outstretched hand. A simple unmarked wooden rowing boat waits to the right on still lapis water, without sail, flags, pennants or banners. Emphasize the emotional tragedy through faces and distance, no assault or blood.
Characters in scene: Nestan matches reference 2, a young olive-skinned royal woman with thick dark hair, dark eyebrows and brown eyes, emerald-and-gold gown, a black veil with gold edging, small emerald head ornament. Davar matches reference 3, a severe mature olive-skinned woman with long dark hair under a maroon-and-gold hood and robe, a small ruby forehead jewel, furrowed brows and a stern expression. Add only the two unnamed attendants needed for the chest; NO Tariel, Parsadan or Asmat.
Story constraints: Tariel and Parsadan are not present at the embarkation. Do not depict Davar’s later suicide or a simultaneous second event. The chest must be large enough to carry a person; it is not a coffin and not a scroll.
Reference 1 is STYLE ONLY, not its poet, courtyard composition or book. References 2 and 3 are IDENTITY ONLY for Nestan and Davar; do not reproduce circular portrait frames. No inset and no second event.
Medieval Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript miniature painting for Shota Rustaveli's "The Knight in the Panther's Skin" (ვეფხისტყაოსანი). 16th–17th-century Georgian royal manuscript miniature, Mamuka Tavakarashvili / King Vakhtang VI illumination tradition blended with classical Persian-Safavid tempera miniature. Egg tempera, lapis lazuli, malachite green, vermilion, warm ochre and burnished antique gold leaf on aged ivory-parchment vellum. Stylized faceted rocky cliffs, ornamental cypress and pomegranate trees, intricately patterned arches and domes, expressive courtly figures in medieval Georgian-Eastern attire. Fine controlled contours, delicately patterned fabrics, luminous matte mineral pigments, slightly flattened layered miniature space with expressive narrative gestures. A painted manuscript scene, not photorealism, cinematic rendering, modern digital fantasy or a collage of circular portraits. Reuse referenced character faces and coloring but adapt costume to the actual chronological story scene; Tariel wears ordinary Indian court or military attire in early backstory, his panther skin belongs to his later exile. Exact horizontal 16:10 composition, preferably native 1600x1000 pixels, a single coherent scene framed for a card vignette. Soft natural painted vignette dissolving to warm aged ivory vellum at edges, modest antique-gold floral flourishes at the perimeter, no rigid border. Key faces and gestures comfortably inside the central safe area, no important content cut off. STRICTLY NO TEXT, NO LETTERS, NO CAPTIONS, NO NUMBERS, NO INSCRIPTIONS, NO CALLIGRAPHY, NO BANNERS, NO SCROLLS, NO SIGNATURES, NO WATERMARKS anywhere. Architectural ornament must be purely floral/geometric with no pseudo-writing. If letters are narratively necessary, use a small closed plain unmarked folded paper or sealed envelope, never visible writing or rolled scrolls. All book covers/pages must be plain and unmarked. Do not show graphic blood or gore; imply violent events through gestures, context and intact clothing.
Mandatory horizontal16:10 painting, ideally native1600x1000. Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, banners or scrolls anywhere.
